name: Quinquaud Folliculitis Decalvans

criteria.description: Presence of cicatricial (scarring) alopecia primarily on the scalp
Follicular pustules and perifollicular erythema with crusting
Isolation of Staphylococcus aureus or other pathogenic bacteria from follicular pustules
Histological evidence of neutrophilic infiltrate around hair follicles with follicular destruction
Chronic relapsing course with progressive hair loss

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of scarring alopecia with follicular pustules and histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by histopathology and bacterial cultures; exclusion of other scarring alopecias is essential.

laboratory: Bacterial culture positive for Staphylococcus aureus
Elevated inflammatory markers during active disease (e.g., ESR, CRP)
imaging: Dermoscopy showing follicular pustules, perifollicular erythema, and tufted hairs
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; possible familial predisposition reported in rare cases
other: Histopathology demonstrating neutrophilic infiltrate and follicular destruction

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of deep nodules and sinus tracts
More common in African descent males
More prominent perifollicular scaling and violaceous erythema

redFlags: Development of abscesses or sinus tracts
Failure to respond to standard antibiotic therapy
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
Wright NA, Messenger AG. Folliculitis decalvans: a review. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2017;76(4):659-665.
